summary: scripts/stack_watchdog.sh now recovers a HUNG core service. A hung service is one whose port has a listener that is its own uvicorn (start-local's `python -m uvicorn <app> --port <port>`, or its reload worker) while /health returns no 200. The existing in-run 30 s debounce is kept; on 2 consecutive runs, plus one more probe right before acting, the watchdog captures diagnostics and runs `./start-local.sh restart <svc>`. Diagnostics go to .logs/hangs/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>-<svc>/: summary.txt (what it saw, ps of each listener, pidfile, established connection count), sample-<pid>.txt (/usr/bin/sample <pid> 3 -file), lsof-<pid>.txt (lsof -nP -p) and log-tail.txt (last 200 lines). Only the newest 10 captures are kept, and only capture-named dirs are ever pruned. Telegram, throttled 30 min per service through the existing tg helper: '<svc> was hung (listening, /health timed out): restarted.' plus the capture path; for an HTTP error it says 'answered HTTP <code>'; a failed restart gets its own alert. Freeze windows: data-service and master-controller are never restarted 07:45-09:20 or 18:30-21:15 IST (ends included); the watchdog alerts instead and restarts on the first hung run after the window. ui-api may be restarted any time. ICICI login: while a Python process runs scripts/daily_session_refresh.py or icici_session_helper.py, no hang restart happens (alert every 15 min): a master-controller tree stop would kill it, the controller relays its OTP, and the login hands its token to ui-api, after which the controller reconnects data-service. A port held by another program (e.g. Docker's forwarder) is reported hourly and never stopped. The hung path replaces the old 'already running' then 'FAILED to start' loop; dead services are started as before. WATCHDOG_DRY_RUN=1 logs the hang decisions only. bash 3.2 compatible; installed atomically. scratch_server.py: the bounded graceful shutdown (3 s) and the lifespan close of the upstream httpx client were already in; added close_timeout=2 on the upstream WebSocket (default 10 s) and a WebSocket SIGTERM regression test. RUNBOOK 'After an outage' gains a 'A hung service' bullet and an `ls -t .logs/hangs` line in the manual recipe.

open_issues: The root cause of the 14:40 ui-api wedge is still unknown. The next hang will leave a capture in .logs/hangs; /usr/bin/sample shows C-level stacks (enough to see a blocked event loop, a lock or a socket read), but not Python frames. py-spy would show them but needs sudo on macOS, so it is not included.
The login deferral has no time limit by design ('never kill a running login'): a login process that never exits blocks every hang restart, with an alert every 15 min.
The freeze and login alerts say '/health not answering' rather than the exact status, because no extra probe is made in those cases.
Pre-existing, theoretical: the watchdog's 20-minute stale-lock window is shorter than a worst-case run (several 300 s start/restart timeouts in one run).

The ownership check relies on start-local.sh's command line containing 'uvicorn' and '--port <port>'. If start_py_service ever changes how it launches uvicorn, listener_is_ours must change with it (test_listener_ownership_is_the_services_own_uvicorn_or_its_child pins the pattern).
